verdict.rationale: Spline documents an official MCP server, bundled in the desktop app, that connects AI coding tools such as Claude, Cursor and Codex directly to the open editor. However, the docs frame it as a way to drive or edit the editor, not as a way for an agent to read design context to implement a design. The Code API is a runtime interactivity library, there is no REST API or OpenAPI spec, and nothing shows retrieval of frames, variables, screenshots or component mappings. Missing for 10: documented read access to frames, variables, screenshots and component-to-code mappings via MCP or API; design-to-code context tooling; independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, my coding agent can pull real design context — frames, variables, screenshots, component mappings — through an MCP server or API to implement the design

citations.quote: The **Spline MCP Server** connects AI coding tools like **Claude**, **Cursor**, **Codex**, and **Antigravity** directly to your Spline editor.
**MCP** support for connecting AI coding tools to your editor
The MCP server is bundled in the desktop app, so connecting Claude, Cursor, VS Code, Antigravity or ChatGPT to your editor only works here
